subject: POC prompt transfer & evaluation SLAs — HarborHealth trial
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@harborhealth.com>, HarborHealth Data Team <data@harborhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC prompt transfer & evaluation SLAs — HarborHealth trial

Hi Sara / HarborHealth data team,

Great to talk earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we can kick off the prompt/label handoff and evaluation pipeline for the trial. Please review and confirm the owners/timing below.

Call recap (high-level)
- Objective: Validate Redwood inference for HarborHealth triage assistant POC (intent classification + structured response generation).
- Scope: 3,000–5,000 prompt examples (mix of single-turn and short multi-turn), expected responses / gold labels for evaluation.
- Requirements: PII-sanitized logs, clear labeling guidance, and a small held-out human-eval set (200 items).

Success criteria (what HarborHealth will use to accept the POC)
- Quality: weighted quality score >= 0.85 (see evaluation plan below; weight intents 60% / response quality 40%).
- Performance: p95 latency <= 500ms for generation at 128-token responses under POC load (test harness to be provided by Redwood).
- Safety: no high-severity hallucinations in a 200-sample human audit.

Required deliverables from HarborHealth (what we need from you)
1) Prompt dataset: CSV with columns: id, user_prompt, system_prompt (optional), conversation_history (optional), expected_response, label_type (categorical/free-text), metadata (JSON string), source_date.
2) Redaction checklist: confirm PII removal strategy (replace PHI with [REDACTED]; retain token-length where possible).
3) Held-out eval set: 200 reviewed examples with human scores / notes.
4) Contact/owner for data upload and access (S3 or Drive).

Redwood owners / next steps (we'll)
- Marcus Lin: ingestion + eval pipeline.
- Priyom Das: prompt normalization and privacy review.
- Olga: commercial/coordination.

Timeline proposal
- Apr 17: HarborHealth uploads full dataset (3–5k rows) + held-out 200 sample set.
- Apr 18–20: Redwood ingests and runs initial automated checks (format, PII heuristics).
- Apr 21–25: Evaluation runs (automated metrics + initial human audit).
- Apr 26: Deliver POC report + recommended config and decision call.

Questions for you (please confirm):
- Will the dataset include system prompts and short conversation history?
- Are you able to accept the redaction guidance above?
- Who will be the point contact for S3 uploads / IAM?

I've attached a sample CSV (harborhealth_prompt_samples_20280410.csv) with the schema we discussed and our standard NDA (NDA_HarborHealth_signed.pdf) — please confirm receipt.

Thanks — if this looks good, please confirm owner and upload ETA.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: harborhealth_prompt_samples_20280410.csv (CSV, 46 KB), NDA_HarborHealth_signed.pdf (PDF, 24 KB)

From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@harborhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Cruz <evan.cruz@harborhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC prompt transfer & evaluation SLAs — HarborHealth trial

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the clear summary — that aligns with what we discussed. A few quick notes and answers:

- We can deliver ~3,200 rows (mix of single-turn and short multi-turn).
- The dataset will include system prompts and the top 1-level conversation history where applicable.
- We will apply PII redaction before transfer. Our policy replaces PHI with token-preserving placeholders (e.g., "John Doe" -> "[REDACTED_PERSON]"). Can you confirm token-preserving placeholders are acceptable?
- We have signed the NDA and attached a copy to this thread.

Owner / upload
- Internal owner: Evan Cruz (evan.cruz@harborhealth.com) — he will coordinate the upload.
- ETA: aiming to upload by EOD Apr 17. If anything slips we’ll push to Apr 18.

Couple of questions for Redwood:
1) For the human audit, do you need any special annotation guidelines or will Redwood provide the rubric?
2) Can you run the eval on Redwood Dedicated (to match expected production latency) or will this be on hosted?

Appreciate it — we’ll confirm when the upload is live.

Best,
Sara Lim
Head of Clinical Product
HarborHealth

Attachments: NDA_HarborHealth_signed.pdf (PDF, 24 KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cruz <evan.cruz@harborhealth.com>, Sara Lim <sara.lim@harborhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC prompt transfer & evaluation SLAs — HarborHealth trial

Thanks Sara — great, and thanks Evan for jumping in. To answer your questions and lock down the plan: 

- Token-preserving placeholders are ideal; if you can use short tags like [REDACTED_NAME] / [REDACTED_MED] that preserves length characteristics we’ll avoid introducing distribution shifts.
- We can run the evaluation on Redwood Dedicated (we'll provision a short-lived test slot that mirrors your expected production config). Marcus will schedule the perf runs.
- For the human audit: Redwood will provide the rubric and annotation interface for the 200-sample review (we prefer to run the audit ourselves to ensure consistency, but can share rubrics if you want to do an internal pass first).

S3 / upload details
- Preferred: presigned S3 upload to our intake bucket. I’ve created one-time presigned path below (expires Apr 18 23:59 UTC):
https://s3-presigned.example.com/harborhealth/hv-2028-042/upload-1
Please upload CSV(s) and a short README (README.txt) describing any metadata column conventions.

Evaluation plan (brief)
- Automated checks: format, schema, PII heuristics, distribution checks (Apr 18).
- Automated metrics: intent accuracy (top-1), response similarity (BLEU/ROUGE), hallucination detectors (Apr 19–21).
- Human audit: 200-sample review scored on 1–5 helpfulness, factuality, and safety (Apr 22–24).
- Final report & config recommendations (Apr 26).

Acceptance pass/fail (example)
- Pass if weighted quality >= 0.85 AND p95 latency <= 500ms AND no >2 high-severity hallucinations in the 200-sample audit.

Owners (confirmed)
- HarborHealth upload: Evan Cruz (external).
- Redwood ingestion & checks: Marcus Lin.
- Redwood eval & human audit: Priyom Das.
- Commercial / escalation: Olga Petrov.

Can you confirm the upload when it’s live and paste the final S3 object path? We’ll start the checks immediately on receipt.

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: harborhealth_prompt_samples_20280410.csv (CSV, 46 KB)

From: Evan Cruz <evan.cruz@harborhealth.com>

Date: Sun, 14 Apr 2028 15:03:00 -07:00

> 
> - Token-preserving placeholders are ideal; if you can use short tags like [REDACTED_NAME] / [REDACTED_MED] that preserves length characteristics we’ll avoid introducing distribution shifts.

Thanks — understood and will apply token-preserving placeholders.

Upload status
- Upload complete. Files uploaded to the presigned link earlier today. Final S3 object path: s3://redwood-intake/harborhealth/hv-2028-042/harbor_prompts_20280414.csv
- Included: harbor_prompts_20280414.csv (3,214 rows), README_upload.txt, heldout_200_sample.csv (200 rows).

Let us know if you need additional fields or an alternate format. Evan is the point for any access/IAM requests.

Thanks,
Evan Cruz
Data Engineering Manager
HarborHealth
